subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these grouped upstream revisions for actions that execute with repository, registry, app-token, scanning, and OpenAI credentials once the exact-head gates are green?
rationale: The patch is mechanically clean, but accepting new third-party executable revisions in secret-bearing workflows is an ownership and supply-chain decision that the protected `security` label intentionally reserves for a human.

options.title: Approve the grouped pins
options.body: Accept all 14 immutable revisions after required exact-head checks pass and an owner confirms the sampled upstream release changes are acceptable.

options.title: Split sensitive action updates
options.body: Separate Codex, app-token, Docker login/build, and CodeQL revisions from setup and maintenance actions for staged approval if the grouped security surface is too broad.

options.title: Pause pending upstream review
options.body: Leave the PR open without merging until owners complete deeper upstream source review for the secret-bearing action revisions.

recommendation.title: Approve the grouped pins
recommendation.body: Accept all 14 immutable revisions after required exact-head checks pass and an owner confirms the sampled upstream release changes are acceptable.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is explicitly connected to the PR and has recent history on the release automation most exposed by these action revisions.
